name: Paleosuchus
sum: Dwarf caimans — the smallest crocodilians of the Americas, two living species in South American rivers, with a few Miocene and Pleistocene fossils.
wsnote: The genus article calls them the smallest crocodilians of the Americas but gives no measurements.
holotype: Living genus — the name-bearing type of the type species is not covered by the sources used.
material: The two living species, plus PBDB occurrences from the Middle Miocene Pebas Formation of Peru and the Late Pleistocene of Brazil; the source also mentions a fossil species that has not been named.
biology: The genus has two living species, the smooth-fronted (Schneider's) dwarf caiman P. trigonatus and Cuvier's dwarf caiman P. palpebrosus, both South American. Unlike other caimans it has no ridge between the eyes and four teeth in each premaxilla instead of five. A 2019 study found evidence of cryptic lineages within P. trigonatus. The name means "ancient crocodile" (Greek palaios + the crocodile god Sobek).
